title: Empirical Benchmark: When Do Theoretical Alignment Axioms Fail?

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: If formal alignment axioms do not hold in practice, theoretical frameworks built on them are grounded in false assumptions. Making violations concrete and measurable is valuable. Bridges theory and practice in alignment.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Designing preference elicitation tasks (forced choice, transitivity tests) is conceptually clear. Uses small models with standard inference. No training required, just prompting and evaluation. Low compute. Accessible for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Multiple axioms to test, multiple model sizes, multiple fine-tuning objectives. The benchmark design is broad. Could be narrowed to one axiom (e.g., transitivity) across 2-3 models. As stated, somewhat broad for 30 hours.
